chunk_findings.detail: `_run` is the shared CLI ask path, but a non-timeout failure still returns `done.unwrap()` and never maps stderr through `_UNAVAILABLE_HINTS` the way `_check` does. Given `gh` installed and not logged in, `P.capture(["gh", ...])` returns non-zero with stderr containing `auth login` / `not logged`; `timed_out` is false, so the caller gets whatever `unwrap()` raises rather than `ForgeUnavailable`. The module contract (and `_check`) treats “could not be asked” as unavailable, not as an ordinary refusal. The earlier refutation does not answer this: its probe describes `gh -f @file` handling, not this return path, and the current `_run` body is unchanged.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge.py:_run

chunk_findings.detail: `_GH_FAILED` / `_GH_OK` omit the CheckRun conclusion `STALE`. Given `statusCheckRollup=[{"status": "COMPLETED", "conclusion": "STALE"}]`, `verdict` is `STALE`, the failing branch is skipped, and the pending clause is false because status is `COMPLETED` and the verdict is not `PENDING`/`EXPECTED`/`""`, so `_gh_checks` returns `"passing"`. A stale check means the head moved or the run was never refreshed; a caller that merges when checks are `"passing"` will merge without a current success.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_github.py:_gh_checks

chunk_findings.detail: `_GH_THREADS_QUERY` asks for `reviewThreads(first:100)` and `threads` never reads `pageInfo` or requests another page. GitHub returns at most 100 nodes. Given PR 5 with 100 already-resolved threads and a 101st unresolved review on the next page, `threads(5)` returns only the first page. A caller that merges when every returned thread is resolved will merge with that open review still on the PR.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_github.py:threads

chunk_findings.detail: `view` attaches line comments only when `review == "changes_requested"`, but `_inline` calls `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/comments` without `--paginate`. That endpoint pages at 30. Given a changes-requested PR whose 31st comment is `src/auth.py:40 alice: this leaks the token`, the join covers only page 1, so `info.feedback` never includes that comment and the actionable review text is dropped.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_github.py:_inline

chunk_findings.detail: After `gh pr create` exits 0, a `find` miss raises `ForgeUnavailable`. That type means the forge was declined or offline. Given a successful create whose `--head` filter does not match (head passed as `refs/heads/feature`, or the new PR not yet visible to `gh pr list`), the adapter reports the forge unavailable even though the PR exists. A caller that retries the whole operation on unavailable will create again on a branch that already has a request.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/forge_github.py:create

chunk_findings.detail: This hunk is the only file in the change, and the stated ratchet is that architecture baselines only shrink. It does the opposite for rows this forge move does not own: `host:[REDACTED:ipv4]` in `ddflow/services/review/model.py` goes from 7 to 14 (line 117), nine new third-party hosts are blessed there (`api.anthropic.com`, `api.openai.com`, `api.x.ai`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, and the rest through `openrouter.ai`), and `["program", "git", "ddflow/services/metrics/lockgit.py", 2]` raises that git count from 1 to 2. A later edit that adds seven more localhost calls in `review/model.py`, a first call to `api.openai.com` from that module, or a second `git` spawn in `lockgit.py` now matches the baseline and the interface ratchet stays green. The superseded rows (PATH in `tree_bin.py`, git in `bugs.py`) are gone; these new allowances are the defect.
